title: 对OpenAI自研芯片的解读与思考
content: OpenAI unveiled Jalapeno, its first self-developed AI inference chip co-created with Broadcom. Manufactured using TSMC's N3P process with HBM4 memory, Jalapeno achieves 1.5-1.9x better power efficiency than NVIDIA's GB300 while consuming only 550-700W. The chip features unified architecture handling both high throughput and low latency without separating prefill/decode tasks, making it ideal for interactive AI agents. Notably, OpenAI completed the design-to-tapeout in just 9 months by using AI to design circuits and write drivers. While NVIDIA's training dominance and CUDA ecosystem remain secure, Jalapeno gives OpenAI negotiating leverage and signals growing challenges to NVIDIA's inference pricing power from major AI companies developing custom silicon.

title: How to evaluate LLMs before production
content: Offline LLM evaluation must evolve beyond benchmarks as systems approach production. GitHub's secret-scanning team reduced false positives 95% by structuring evaluations around product decisions rather than isolated metrics. Key practices include: defining primary outcomes, safety constraints, and operational guardrails; treating evaluation as repeatable integration testing with versioned components; keeping offline conditions close to production realism; treating production labels critically; supplementing with synthetic data; performing error analysis to identify failure patterns; and using LLM-as-judge for triage rather than ground truth.
